newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay police nail strike violence rumours.
newsitem.headline: Bombay police nail strike violence rumours.

text.p: Bombay police on Monday denounced rumours that prominent political leaders had been killed in violence sparked off by an ongoing strike to protest the death of 12 people in police firing last week.
"There are many wild rumours going through the city," said a police official. "But apart from a few stray incidents of stone-throwing, there has been no large-scale trouble."
Police officials specifically denied rumours that the leaders of some opposition political parties had been killed.
The rumours have prompted many offices in the city to shut early.

Some train services have been however disrupted. A Central Railway spokesman told Reuters that trains between Kurla and Thane stations on the suburban railway network had been halted for more than three hours by intermittent incidents of stone-throwing.
"In many places people have pulled sleepers onto the tracks, or are sitting on the rails," he said.
Thousands of commuters who rely on the trains to get to work each day found themselves stranded. They had to get off and walk along the tracks to the nearest railway station.
